title: Chapter 25: Unlocking a New Scenario
html:
Several used cotton swabs, a bottle of mineral water, and an unopened bun sat on the wooden table.

The young officer across from Chen Ge set down his recorder and held up a photograph on his phone. “Is this one of the men you saw?”

The picture showed several men leaving a building together. The tallest had a peony tattoo on the back of one hand.

“Yes. That’s him.”

“His name is Zhang Peng. He has substantial gambling debts and is already wanted in connection with several other offenses.” The officer swiped to another image. “Now look at this one.”

The second image appeared to come from a traffic camera. After zooming in, Chen Ge recognized the driver as the heavyset man from Ping An Apartments.

“That looks like him.”

“Your description matched a man named Feng Chunlei, who is also wanted in connection with an earlier traffic offense.” The officer put away his phone and straightened the papers in front of him. “I have what I need for now, Mr. Chen, but the main investigation team will want a more complete statement from you. You’re an important witness, so please cooperate with them.”

“Of course.” Chen Ge leaned back against the bed as the adrenaline slowly ebbed. A few hours earlier, the Western Jiujiang police station had received an urgent report concerning Ping An Apartments and dispatched officers immediately. They encountered Chen Ge on the road and, after hearing his account, split into two teams.

One team followed him back toward the wooden cabin to look for Wang Qi; the other searched for the tenants who had fled into the hills. By the time they reached the cabin, Wang Qi was already gone, though the scene made it obvious that something serious had happened there.

The officers also found the clothing Chen Ge had described, which was enough to trigger a much larger search of the area.

As the key witness, Chen Ge was placed under police protection. The officers initially wanted to take him straight to the station, but the black phone’s mission still required him to remain at Ping An Apartments until morning. He insisted that additional evidence might still be inside the building and persuaded them to take his statement there.

So Chen Ge lay on the bed in his temporary room with officers stationed nearby, waiting for the mission timer to expire.

At 3:00 a.m., the door opened and a middle-aged officer in his forties stepped inside. He removed his cap, picked up the water bottle from the table, and took a long drink.

“Uncle Sanbao, that’s mine.” Chen Ge sat up when he recognized him. Li Sanbao was the deputy head of the Western Jiujiang police station and had also been involved in the case surrounding Chen Ge’s parents’ disappearance. During that difficult period, he had been one of the adults who regularly checked in on Chen Ge.

“You little brat. How many times have I told you not to call me Uncle Sanbao while I’m working? It’s Superintendent Li—or Inspector Li.” Li Sanbao set down the bottle, unable to hide a smile. “I’ll let it slide today. You’ve done something genuinely useful for once.”

Chen Ge sat up straighter. “Did you catch him?”

“Don’t underestimate the investigation team. They found Wang Qi and most of the people from the apartments. Zhang Peng is the only one still missing.”

“That’s great news.”

“They also located the remains believed to be Wang Qi’s fiancée, and the forensic team is examining the evidence now. If you have questions, ask them quickly. I still have work to do.” Inspector Li had stopped by mainly to reassure him that the search was making progress.

“Zhang Peng and Feng Chunlei were already wanted. What about the other two?” Chen Ge asked.

“The woman is Zhang Peng’s wife, so investigators will determine how much she knew and what role she played. The landlord is more complicated. He originally worked as the old man’s caretaker, then joined the others in taking control of the property. We haven’t found evidence that he physically abused the old man, though.” Inspector Li put his cap back on. “Why do you ask?”

“Just curious.” Remembering He San’s advice, Chen Ge gave him his most innocent smile. “Although… I’ve heard there are sometimes rewards for helping the police locate wanted suspects?”

“We’ll mail you a commendation banner when the case is closed. Goodbye.”

“Hey, wait!”

The younger officer laughed after Inspector Li left. “He’s teasing you. If Wang Qi is confirmed as the person responsible for the old case, there may be a government reward of around thirty thousand yuan. The elderly owner also offered five thousand yuan for information related to his family’s deaths.”

“So there really is a cash reward?” Chen Ge’s eyes brightened. “Not that money had anything to do with why I helped, of course. Contributing to the peace and safety of this wonderful city is reward enough.”

The young officer smiled but wisely chose not to comment. He returned to his post by the door.

Later, after the investigation team finished questioning him, the officers offered to take Chen Ge home. He came up with excuse after excuse to remain in the building until dawn—he needed to retrieve something from Room 208, he wanted to clarify where he had found certain evidence, and so on. Only at 6:00 a.m., when the black phone finally displayed its Mission Complete notification, did he agree to leave in a police car.

Watching the scenery pass outside the window, Chen Ge felt surprisingly awake. He discreetly took out the black phone and checked his reward.

“Player arrived at the mission location on time, identified the person responsible for the murders, and remained until dawn. Trial Mission: Murder by Midnight—complete! A new scenario has been unlocked. The player may now use the phone interface to control props within the scenario.”

“Trial Mission completion rate exceeded ninety percent. Congratulations! Hidden reward unlocked: Wang Qi’s Missing-Person Notice.”

“Wang Qi’s Missing-Person Notice (11 Malice Points): Every day, I search for the love I destroyed. I try to bury the past, but it always finds me again. Every morning, reminders of her appear beside me. I hid her away, yet somehow she still lives inside my heart.”
